_doc: Signal types and their plain-language explanation (shown by the i button). lag_months = typical months from signal to tender, used by the prediction rules; null = no auto prediction.

Budget.explanation: Money approved for a programme in a fiscal year (PSDP, ADP, USF). Funded schemes must spend it, so tenders usually follow within the same fiscal year (July–June).

Policy / roadmap.explanation: A government strategy or masterplan that sets direction but no money yet. Tenders come later, once projects are carved out and funded: typically 6–24 months.

Law.explanation: An Act passed by the National Assembly or a provincial assembly. It creates obligations (for example, mandatory digital payments) that departments must buy systems to meet.

Regulation.explanation: Rules issued under a law or by a regulator (PPRA, PTA, SBP, NADRA). They change how buying happens or what buyers must comply with.

Loan approval.explanation: A World Bank, ADB or other lender has approved or cleared financing. The lender publishes a procurement plan; specific tenders follow in 3–12 months.

Donor facility.explanation: A pooled fund that countries apply to project by project. Each approved project becomes a new procurement pipeline.

Donor dialogue.explanation: Early talks between the government and a lender. No money yet; useful 12+ months ahead to shape requirements.

Pipeline.explanation: A project at concept or appraisal stage with a lender or the Planning Commission. Good time to meet the client before specs are written.

Project update.explanation: Progress or new scope on a project already funded. Often signals an add-on package or the next phase.

Ministerial announcement.explanation: A minister or chief minister announces an initiative or deadline. Creates urgency; check whether money is behind it.

Market.explanation: A competitor, partner or private investment. Not a tender, but it changes JazzWorld's position.
